content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This work proposes a method called FreeSeg for mask-free learning of open-vocabulary semantic segmentation using image-text model pre-training. The method builds on top of the Interpretable-CLIP (ICLIP) method and proposes a number of modifications to obtain better pseudo-labels masks from it. Specifically it (a) smooths the predicted image tokens via a spatial average filter, (b) performs a minimum pooling of the spatial tokens and use it (somehow) to better segment the background regions and (c) after the zero-shot mask prediction stage further trains a PSPNet with mask pseudo-labels with dense CRF for post processing. The proposed method is compared against the state-of-the-art GroupViT method on the Pascal VOC and MS COCO datasets. The authors also show ablations studies to understand the improvements brought out by their various design components.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths: The paper addresses the largely unexplored open and important problem of label-efficient semantic segmentation via leveraging the good generalization ability of large image-text pre-trained models.

Weaknesses:
1. Clarity: The paper requires a major editorial revision to get it to an acceptable level. In its current form it is simply incomprehensible and requires several re-reads to parse the text. I list some issues below. However, this list is, by no means, a comprehensive one. Beyond the issues listed below, the authors are very strongly encouraged to review and fix the entire paper for editorial issue.
- director --> more direct
- indicates inner production between --> indicates inner product between
- "semantic shift between foregrounds and backgrounds." What does this mean? Explain.
- "Masked Max Pooling (MMP) as Fig. 2," --> There is not MMP module in Fig. 2
- "mean attention map A" --> What is this? It is not defined.
- It is never defined in the method how $F_c$ is actually used in the contrastive loss.
- confidential --> confident
- Unclear sentence "Our motivation is to mitigate those highly similar image-text pixel pairs, and thus reduce the contract between
most discriminative region and other parts."
- Unclear sentence "Thanks to the existent of extra projections of ICLIP and the proposed smoothing operation, min
pooling is able to learn the non-partial representations, without interfere to the classification branch."
- "mMIoU" used before defining it
- Which results in Table 1 are for "dense ITSM"?
- Table 2-5: indicate what dataset these results are on.

2. Conceptual Novelty: The paper doesn't provide new fundamental technical insights to advance research in the field of using text-image models for zero-shot mask-free segmentation. It presents is a collection of engineering tricks designed to improve accuracy numbers, including smoothing of the spatial tokens, min pooling of token to get the background, plausible label selection to limit argmax to the top higher probably labels, PSPNet training with pseudo-labels, dense CRF and boundary pixel engineering. These engineering ideas are obvious and can be applied to other competing methods such as GroupViT, as well. They are not unique to proposed method and hence and don't provide any new task specific insights.

3. Comparisons to GroupViT
(a) Accuracy comparisons. This work mis-quotes the accuracy of the competing SOTA work GroupViT in Tables 6 and 7 for the PASCAL VOC and MS COCO datasets. The original GroupViT has no stage 2 with dataset-specific training, advanced segmentation network or dense CFR-based refinement, but only a stage 1 for direct zero-shot inference on the validation sets of VOC and COCO. The numbers reported for GroupViT's accuracy for training on 28M images in this paper under the Stage 2 column are in fact the accuracies of its stage 1.  GroupViT's stage 1 accuracy on PASCAL VOC is 52.3 and for MS COCO is 24.3 -- both of these numbers are higher than the proposed methods' stage 1 accuracies. Additionally, for the author's re-training of GroupViT with the 3M dataset, it is unclear whether its weights were initialized with DINO as well as was done for the proposed method? If not, for a fair comparison, could the authors provide the results of their method trained on GCC with their image encoder initialized from scratch versus from DINO?

(b) The authors claim "These extra projections are designed for independent representations of
interpretability task, which is much simpler than GroupViT Xu et al. (2022) in architecture." In what way is the proposed method simpler? Can the authors provide a quantitative comparison of the computational cost of their two stage approach of (VitB + PSPNet) against that of GroupViT's single image encoder?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: Poor. The paper requires a major editorial revision to make it comprehensible. 

Quality: The overall quality of the work is sub-par in terms of technical novelty, clarity and significance of results.

Novelty: No fundamental technical insights. Mostly engineering tricks.

Reproducibility: Partially reproducible. The method is hard to follow because of editorial issues. No code is provided. Partial implementation details are provided in the experiment section.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall this paper does not offer new technical insights to fundamentally advance research in zero-shot text-image model guided semantic segmentation; is lacking in presentation quality and does not outperform the SOTA works in terms of accuracy or computational cost. Hence I recommend rejecting this paper.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a method to segment a novel class object in a zero-shot manner, using text supervision. Starting from ICLIP, the authors improve the performance with some modifications (smoothed min pooling, partial label strategy, partial pixel strategy). The proposed method achieves significant performance improvements on the Pascal VOC and Ms COCO datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength

++ The proposed techniques are simple, so I guess they can be easily implemented.

++ The proposed techniques bring meaningful improvements over baselines.

++ Ablation studies are quite well conducted

Weakness

-- In my opinion, the novelty of this paper is limited. The overall structure heavily depends on ICLIP, and the two main contributions, smoothed min pooling and partial label strategy, are already explored in the previous works. 

1) For smoothed min pooling, the authors argue minimum pooling is hardly used in previous works, but the similar pooling technique is already used in weakly supervised learning. [A] only considers non-discriminative regions (whose scores are low) for pooling.

[A] Lee, Jungbeom, et al. "Reducing information bottleneck for weakly supervised semantic segmentation.", NeurIPS 2021.

2) For partial label strategy, [B] already used a similar technique to suppress the scores of the classes that are unlikely in the image.

[B] Wei, Yunchao, et al. "Object region mining with adversarial erasing: A simple classification to semantic segmentation approach.", CVPR 2017.

-- It is pretty challenging to understand some parts. 

1) The proposed technique heavily depends on ICLIP, so the explanation of ICLIP should be more sophisticated. Why are there multiple texts N_t? Why mean attention map A is multiplied? 

2) High-level explanation of mMIoU would give better understanding of the metric.

-- In Table 6, the performance of GroupViT is sensitive to the number of data samples. I wonder how FreeSeg can be improved by using the larger dataset.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper address an interesting problem, zero-shot segmentation without explicit segmentation labels. The proposed techniques are simple and effective. However, my major concern is the limited novelty of the proposed techniques. Therefore, I vote for an rejection for this submission.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper proposes FreeSeg, a novel technique to perform open-world semantic segmentation. FreeSeg performs segmentation without annotations relying on a pretrained dense ICLIP (interpretable CLIP) model. In particular, the paper first proposes to train ICLIP with increased resolution and Smoothed Min Pooling (SMP), which helps the model highlight all the objects' discriminative regions. Once obtained the dense ICLIP model, the paper proposes to extract partial segmentation labels from it to train a downstream segmentation model. Since using argmax operation on the CLIP output would be too noisy, the paper introduces a filtering operation, first on the classes appearing on the image and then on the confidence of the pixels.
FreeSeg demonstrates superior performance to comparable methods on the Pascal-VOC and COCO datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strenght:
The paper proposes an exciting method that may enormously reduce the cost of segmentation models in the future. The approach is an extension of the previous ICLIP model adapted for the segmentation task. 

Weaknesses:
1. The paper is missing a comparison with weakly-supervised baselines, even in an adapted form. In principle, the proposed FreeSeg framework is comparable to the image-level weakly-supervised approach. To be clear, current weakly supervised methods, starting from image-level labels, train a classification network to extract pseudo-supervision and then train a downstream segmentation network. We can relate their framework to FreeSeg by considering the use of CLIP to extract (pseudo) image-level labels for the training images. However, the current image-level supervised approaches are able to outperform the FreeSeg framework by a large margin (see https://paperswithcode.com/sota/weakly-supervised-semantic-segmentation-on for multiple references). It would be important to consider these comparisons and show that the segmentation masks extracted from ICLIP are better than the ones extracted from a segmentation network to strengthen the contribution.
2. The pseudo-label construction of FreeSeg is highly engineered and requires setting four thresholds: a background threshold t and its delta (Eq. 9), the strict and loose thresholds in Eq. 8. However, the paper does not illustrate how to select these thresholds and how robust the method is at their variations. 
3. In Table 5 is reported an interesting result: using the Dense ITSM and partial label performs worse than using only partial label. Is there any explanation for this behavior? Moreover, the Table does not report SMP + Partial Labels. Following the previous observation, I would expect it to be superior to Dense ITSM + SMP + Partial Labels.

Additional comments:
1. There is a typo on page 6, Line 1: "we record the all the predicted ... ". 
2. IoU is wrongly extended as Inter of Union. mIoU is "mean Intersection over Union" and mMIoU is "mean Match Intersection over Union".
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is clear and reports a novel and interesting method.
The paper reports the most important hyper-parameters to replicate the experiments.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper presents a novel and interesting framework. However, it lacks important comparisons with a related research field that is very important to highlight. Moreover, the paper does not provide information on how to tune important hyper-parameters.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
